[PATH:theoretical] Analytic study of the map's Lyapunov exponents or drift analysis using a probabilistic model (e.g., assuming independence of residues and computing expected log growth) — If the expected log growth under a suitable stochastic model is positive for some residue classes, that suggests the possibility of divergence, contradicting the universal attractor hypothesis. [PATH:literature] Literature review of known results on similar piecewise linear maps (e.g., Collatz-type maps with mod 3 cases) and their known attractor structures, particularly those with proven universal attractors or proven divergence — Existing rigorous results on related maps (e.g., the 3x+1 problem, generalized Collatz functions) can provide analogous proof techniques or counterexamples.
